extracted.intended_audience: heads of departments and agencies, federal procurement officials, and interested commenters/parties
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on rescission of OMB A-49
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting comments and understanding procedural requirements related to the proposed rescission of OMB Circular No. A-49 (Use of Management and Operating Contracts), and related procedural rules for intervention in NRC licensing/amendment proceedings referenced on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed rescission rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Action to rescind OMB Circular No. A-49 is based on the recommendation of the Assistant Secretaries for Management Group (Reform 88 Program) and an assessment that other existing policies and regulations provide adequate guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice states that procurement requirements and policies have changed, that the Circular's provisions are reflected in more recently updated regulations (e.g., FAR Subpart 17A) and policy documents (e.g., OFPP Policy Letter 84-1), and therefore Circular A-49 is not necessary and should be rescinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission requirements for the rescission notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties are invited to comment on the proposed rescission; comments should include reference to the Notice and be sent to the named OFPP contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should include reference to this Notice and be sent to: Mr. Robert C. Blenvenoe, Office of Federal Procurement Policy, Washington, DC 20503. The notice specifies that comments must be received 60 days from the date of the notice; an internal routing memo also requests comments be received by this Office on or before December 31, 1985 (and notes an extension in one place).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-49 scope and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular No. A-49 (Feb 25, 1959) established general criteria to assist Executive agencies in developing policies for the use of management and operating contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management and operating contracts are described as being used to administer research and development establishments; to administer and operate Government-owned or leased industrial facilities; or to perform such personal or professional services as are authorized by law. The Circular is said to have limited applicability to Executive agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement/updated guidance for M&O contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies previously stated in Circular A-49 have been restated or superseded in more recent acquisition regulations and OFPP guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice cites the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 17A, and OFPP Policy Letter 84-1 (Federally Funded Research and Development Centers) as more current authorities and guidance addressing management and operating contract issues and the funding vehicle role for FFRDCs/FFR&DCs and federal laboratories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for leave to intervene — specificity requirements (10 CFR 2.714)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for leave to intervene must set forth with particularity the interest of the petitioner in the proceeding and how that interest may be affected by the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition should specifically explain reasons why intervention should be permitted and make particular reference to these factors: (1) the nature of the petitioner's right under the Act to be made a party; (2) the nature and extent of the petitioner's property, financial or other interest in the proceeding; and (3) the possible effect of any order which may be entered in the proceeding on the petitioner's interest. The petition should also identify the specific aspects of the subject matter of the proceeding as to which the petitioner wishes to intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and supplemental petition deadlines (NRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural timing for amendments and supplements to petitions in NRC licensing/amendment proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who has filed a petition for leave to intervene (or who has been admitted) may amend the petition without requesting leave of the Board up to fifteen (15) days prior to the first prehearing conference. No later than fifteen (15) days prior to the first prehearing conference, a petitioner shall file a supplement to the petition which must include a list of the contentions to be litigated and the bases for each contention set forth with reasonable specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contentions requirements (NRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contentions in a petition/supplement must be narrowly framed and supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contentions shall be limited to matters within the scope of the amendment under consideration. The supplement must include the contentions sought to be litigated and the bases for each contention with reasonable specificity. A petitioner who fails to file such a supplement which satisfies these requirements with respect to at least one contention will not be permitted to participate as a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and limitations of intervenors
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences and procedural rights for parties permitted to intervene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those permitted to intervene become parties to the proceeding, subject to any limitations in the order granting leave to intervene, and have the opportunity to participate fully in the conduct of the hearing, including the opportunity to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing location and emergency/late-filing procedure (NRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where and how to file petitions and how to notify the Commission if filings occur during the last ten days of the notice period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for a hearing or petition for leave to intervene shall be filed with the Secretary of the Commission, U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Washington, D.C., Attention: Docketing and Service Branch, or may be delivered to the Commission's Public Document Room, 1717 H Street NW, Washington, D.C. If petitions are filed during the last ten (10) days of the notice period, the petitioner or representative is requested to promptly inform the Commission by a toll-free Western Union datagram (provide Datagram Identification Number 3737) with specified message contents (petitioner's name and telephone number, date petition was mailed, plant name, publication date and page number of the Federal Register notice). A copy of the petition should also be sent to the Executive Legal Director, U.S. NRC and to the attorney for the licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nontimely filings policy (NRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on consideration of late petitions, amended petitions, supplemental petitions, or requests for hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nontimely filings will not be entertained absent a determination by the Commission, the presiding officer, or the presiding Atomic Safety and Licensing Board that the petition and/or request should be granted based upon a balancing of factors specified in 10 CFR 2.714(b)(1)(i) and 2.714(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to obtain application materials and further details
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of the underlying application and supplements for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For further details see the application for amendment dated February 27, 1985, as supplemented June 10, June 28, and July 11, 1985; these documents are available for public inspection at the Commission's Public Document Room, 1717 H Street NW, Washington, D.C., and at the local/regional library identified in the notice.
